answers: Things have felt pretty settled. Last week I swapped one of my late shifts for an earlier shift, which meant my partner and I could go to a concert together. That was a real highlight of the week. I’m still enjoying my work at the venue. I’d like to work out how to fit future appointments around my shifts a bit more easily.

I’d like to work out when I can come to appointments so they fit better with my work shifts. I put both on the same wall calendar. Agreeing on appointment dates ahead of time would help me know how my week will look.
Do you mean how many hours of sleep I’m actually getting, or whether I’ve had trouble getting to sleep or staying asleep?
I haven’t felt especially unsettled lately. I do find it irritating when a plan changes at the last minute, because I like to have my week laid out. Overall, though, things have felt settled.

I keep one wall calendar and put my appointments and my work shifts on it together, so I can see how the week is laid out. It helps to agree on appointment dates ahead of time so I can plan around work.
I put the dates and times of my shifts on the wall calendar, and do the same for appointments. That lets me see where an appointment fits alongside the shifts.
Do you mean having the week organized? If I have a fairly good idea what the week is going to look like, I find it easier to fit work and treatment together. For me that’s one part of staying well.

For me it’s enjoying work and still having time to spend with my partner and enjoy music. The concert we went to last week is a good example. I like having something to look forward to as well as having the week organized.
My partner. I like being able to spend time together after I’ve finished work. Going to the concert together last week was a real highlight for me.
“After a long event at the venue, I take ten quiet minutes to stack the chairs before I head home. I like that part of the routine because it gives me time to unwind before I leave work.”
